### Observed differences

- In the later window, A02 appears in about 65 in 100 traces instead of about 21 in 100, and its mean occurrences per trace rise from 0.22 to 0.70. Its position shifts from about 57% of the trace to about 92%, and it now usually occurs after A45 and before A46. [OCC001, POS001, REL009, REL010, DIR001, DIR011, LAG002, LAG012]
- A06 appears less often, falling from about 21 in 100 traces to about 7 in 100. Its successor distribution also changes: A44, which was about 31% of A06 transitions, is no longer observed as a successor. [OCC002, DIR002]
- In the middle segment, A21 and A22 now lead to A23/A24 instead of A30: A21→A30 drops from about 51% to 2%, and A22→A30 from about 45% to 1%. A23 and A24 now lead almost exclusively to A30, about 94% and 97% respectively. A29 now leads to A21/A22 in about 98% of its transitions, instead of spreading across A21/A22/A23/A24. Lag evidence indicates a sequence A29 → A21/A22 → A23/A24 → A30. [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011]
- A45 now often goes to A02, about 63% of the time, instead of A46, which falls from about 84% to 36%. [DIR011, REL009, REL010, LAG013]
- A14 and A15 successors become more concentrated: A14→A15 rises from about 85% to 98.5%, and A15→A16 from about 94% to 97.5%. [DIR003, DIR004]
- A22 before A24 increases from about 10% to 30.5% of traces. [REL011]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, A02 is executed much more often and is inserted near the end of the trace, after A45 and before A46, in a large share of cases. It also supports a reordering in the A21/A22/A23/A24/A29/A30 segment, from a mixed order to a more fixed sequence A29 → A21/A22 → A23/A24 → A30. The occurrence, position, direct-successor, co-occurrence and lag indicators agree on these placements. A competing explanation based only on sampling differences in variant frequencies is unlikely to account for the number and consistency of the observed items, although some individual lag items have small support and the A06 decrease may reflect a separate or related branch reduction. [OCC001, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, DIR001, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR011, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011, LAG013]
